title: Scalar reduction of the inverse diagonal base-change mate
statement: Fix the finite purity conventions [def-pur-conventions] and the actual comparisons [def-pur-finite-diagonal-reduction-comparisons]. Let f:X to Y be separated, quasi-compact, locally of finite type and smooth of pure relative dimension d over the algebraically closed base field k, with Y separated of finite type. Let A=A_E,n and B=A_E,m for 1<=m<=n, and Q be derived scalar extension. Use the source and normal sections of the diagonal and the root-line conventions [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The inverse diagonal base-change factor a_R: omega_f,R to C_R(p1,Delta) satisfies q_C Q(a_A)=a_B q_omega. This concerns only the normalized base-change mate, not the DNC or vector factor. Identity reductions, d=0, empty schemes and arbitrary ramification are included.

proof.text:
the inverse smooth base-change map is the adjunction mate of the pullback
base-change square. Apply scalar extension to its unit-and-counit formula and use
scalar pullback balancing and reduced-counit compatibility. The same triangle
identities identify the two resulting mates. Pull along the diagonal, whose
composite with the first projection is the identity, and insert the coefficient-unit
and intrinsic realization comparisons. These are exactly omegaMap and
diagonalSectionMap, so the inverse-alpha square commutes. The argument uses no
orientation and works in relative dimension zero and for identity reductions.

theorem diagonalBaseChangeReduction :
      (proScalar (quotient P m hm hmn) X).map (P.chartDiagonalAlpha d f aY).inv ≫
        diagonalSectionMap P m hm hmn d f aY =
      omegaMap P m hm hmn f aY ≫
        ((P.finiteReductionSetting m hm).chartDiagonalAlpha d f aY).inv
